text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices makes your API easier to use and maintain. First, choose clear and meaningful endpoint names that reflect the resources they represent. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand whether a request succeeded or failed. Third, provide complete documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Fourth, use versioning in your URL, such as /v1/, so you can improve the API without breaking existing applications. Finally, keep your design simple and consistent. A well-designed API saves developers time and reduces errors, which leads to happier users and fewer support requests.
